A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EDTR paper and complete supplementary Sections S1–S12. All scientific text, equations, figures, and tables are identical and available for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EDTR classification, segmentation, and detection experiments, including benchmark results, ablations, generalization studies, and supplementary measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including Table 1, the main-text ablations and generalization studies, and supplementary Tables S1–S7.

M1.justification: The EDTR architecture, pre-restoration, partial diffusion, short-step denoising, losses, and alternating training procedure in Section 3 and Algorithm S1 are identical.

E1.justification: Dataset, task, and scenario coverage is identical, including CUB200, PASCAL VOC2012, Tiny-ImageNet†, StanfordCars, RealPhoto60 examples, and the Mixture-A/B degradation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Table 1 retains SwinIR, TDSR, RSRSSN, SR4IR, and the oracle/no-restoration controls; the supplementary DiffBIR and SR4IR+SD comparisons are also identical.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, degradation procedures, model configurations, training budgets, and generalization protocols in Sections 4, S1, and S2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain identical component and denoising-step ablations, cross-task and unseen-dataset analyses, feature-space visualizations, pre-restoration comparisons, decoder/color-correction ablations, and qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Section S7 and Table S4 retain mean/standard-deviation reporting over 10 inference runs, four-inference averaging for task performance, and single-inference image-quality reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are identical. For example, Table 1 retains Mixture-B EDTR-1step classification accuracy of 68.8% and EDTR-4step detection mAP of 31.9%.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, diffusion definitions, Equations (1)–(10), and mathematical operations in Algorithm S1 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about using tailored diffusion designs to improve task performance and visual quality under complex degradation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning redundant details from longer denoising, complementary feature spaces, PSNR versus task performance, and generalization are unchanged. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added or revised.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is identical, including optimization settings, training iterations, batch sizes, hardware, Algorithm S1, and baseline reimplementation details. Code/data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to SR4IR and UniRestore, and all 71 bibliographic entries are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1, 30 Jul 2025 to v2, 2 Sep 2025. Body wording, title, authors, headings, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and page arrangements are unchanged, including the supplementary material. Pages 2–18 render identically; the first-page difference is confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The complete scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and supplementary material are identical. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp, its link, and PDF metadata produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
